prompt:
Clean HD painterly chibi 2D RPG animation sheet, NOT pixel art, of the EXACT character in Image 1 (Yuki, the Snow-Moon Empress: rabbit ears, white braided hair, opal-white crystal armour, deep blue cape, a tall upright staff topped with a large blue CRESCENT MOON held in the hand on the RIGHT side of the image, and a radiant ice FAN held in the other hand in front of her body). Keep her identity, colours, face, armour, staff and fan exactly.
Image 2 is the current sheet: EXACTLY the same layout (3 columns x 2 rows, six 512x512 cells, landscape 1536x1024), the same character size, the same position in every cell, the same feet line. Change only the arms and the fan as described.
THE BASIC ATTACK: she casts a FAN GUST at the enemy on the right. Facing RIGHT, three-quarter view.
THE STAFF HAND (on the right side of the image) holds the crescent staff upright with ONE hand in EVERY frame, exactly as in Image 1: same grip, the staff perfectly still and vertical. There is only ever ONE hand on the staff; no second hand on the staff in any frame.
THE FAN HAND does the attack:
Frame 1: ready, exactly like Image 1 (fan held in front of her body).
Frame 2: she draws the fan back toward her opposite shoulder, fan half closed, body coiling slightly.
Frame 3: she sweeps the fan forward and open, mid-swing in front of her chest.
Frame 4: full release: the fan wide open, arm extended forward toward the RIGHT (toward the enemy), body leaning slightly into it.
Frame 5: the fan coming back toward her body.
Frame 6: back to the ready pose of Frame 1.
No effects, no wind, no snowflakes, no glow: body, staff and fan only. Nothing crosses a cell edge.
Uniform pure flat #FF00FF magenta background, no text, no labels, no borders, no grid lines, no floor, no shadows.

No cut-off limbs, text, extra figures or fused hands are visible. The sheet is about 1024x683 rather than the 1536x1024 the prompt requested, but that is not a listed defect. Single-hand staff grip and exact pose timing could not be fully verified at this resolution.
